clue.text: Firmly secured or escaped

definitions.meaning: fastened shut with a bolt, as a door is
ran off suddenly, as a horse does from its stable

explanation.definitionFit: A word with opposite-feeling senses: fastened tight with a bolt, or made a sudden dash for freedom.

clue.text: British case I misrepresented in European city

indicators.note: letters misrepresented are shown in a false order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A British legal case gets distorted somewhere on the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'British' looks like an adjective for 'case', but it gives its own abbreviation; 'misrepresented' rearranges CASE and I into ESCIA; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Brescia is a city in Lombardy, northern Italy, hence a European city.

clue.text: Volume of literature with 50% cut out

indicators.note: letters cut out of the word literature are removed from it, here five of its ten

explanation.surface: A book of literature has half its pages excised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with 50%' says how much goes: five of the ten letters (E, A, T, U, R, scattered) are 'cut out', not a clean front or back half, leaving L, I, T, R, E.
explanation.definitionFit: A litre is a metric unit of capacity, so it measures a volume.

clue.text: Cost of stocking river with some swans

indicators.note: to stock something is to fill it, so the river holds the swans inside it

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, south-west England
pens are female swans, so several of them are PENS

explanation.surface: How much it costs to populate a river with a few swans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stocking' is a verb here, meaning filling, not hosiery; a pen is a female swan, a fact solvers may not know.
explanation.definitionFit: An expense is an outlay of money, so it is a cost.

clue.text: Academics accepting old work of mathematicians

indicators.note: the academics take something in, so another piece goes inside them

parts.note: profs is a casual short form for professors

explanation.surface: University staff take on an old piece of mathematical research.
explanation.definitionFit: Mathematicians spend their days writing proofs, rigorous demonstrations that a theorem holds.

clue.text: Planted firmly in ground or removed from it

definitions.meaning: having taken root, fixed in the earth
dug or pulled up, as a pig roots up the soil

explanation.definitionFit: The word can mean firmly fixed by roots, or, from rooting out, torn up from the earth.

clue.text: Careful checking or careless mistake

definitions.meaning: supervision, watching over something
an omission made through failing to notice something

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both supervisory watchfulness and an error of not noticing.

clue.text: Put on outer cover or removed outer cover

definitions.meaning: covered with a skin or surface layer
stripped of its skin, as a rabbit is before cooking

explanation.definitionFit: The verb skin can mean to cover with a layer, or to peel off the hide.

clue.text: It could be folded once, or twice — it's ambiguous

definitions.text: It could be folded once, or twice — it's ambiguous

parts.words: It could be folded once, or twice — it's ambiguous
parts.note: folded once is doubled, and something with two senses at once is ambiguous; the clue plays on a phrase for a word read two ways

explanation.walkthrough: The clue is itself about the whole puzzle: every other clue rests on a word with two opposed senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase or word with two possible interpretations has a dual sense, which makes it ambiguous.

clue.text: Disappeared or remaining

definitions.meaning: went away, departed
still there after the rest has gone

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both departed and still remaining behind, two opposed senses.

clue.text: Got one chip wrong, but generally producing good shots

indicators.note: the letters are put together wrongly, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A golfer mishits a chip shot, though usually plays well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges GOT, ONE and CHIP. 'Shots' suggests golf, but they are photographs.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone photogenic looks good in photographs, so pictures of them usually turn out well.

clue.text: Show or hide

definitions.meaning: to project or broadcast
to shield from view

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to display a film and to conceal something behind a barrier.

clue.text: Book by female author bringing good fortune

parts.note: Doris Lessing was a British novelist and Nobel laureate

explanation.surface: A novel by a woman writer brings its reader luck.
explanation.definitionFit: A blessing is a stroke of luck or something beneficial, so good fortune.

clue.text: Commercial vehicle's indicator showing damage

definitions.meaning: the device in a cab that shows the fare
damage is slang for the cost, as in 'what's the damage?'

explanation.definitionFit: A meter in a hired cab displays the fare owed, the cost or 'damage'.

clue.text: Cases resulting from incessant misbehaving

indicators.note: letters misbehaving are out of order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Lawsuits arising from someone's constant bad conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: Instances and cases are synonyms, both meaning examples or occurrences.

clue.text: Part for tragedian like King Lear

indicators.note: only part of the word tragedian is used, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: An actor in tragedy takes on the role of Shakespeare's Lear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part' takes a run from inside TRAGEDIAN; 'for' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Lear is a very old king in Shakespeare's play, so an elderly man like him is old.

clue.text: Of highest quality, or worst

definitions.meaning: finest, top, superlative of good
as a verb, to worst is to defeat someone

explanation.definitionFit: The word is the superlative of good, and also a verb meaning to defeat or get the better of.

clue.text: Prison and one of its occupants?

parts.note: a brig is a ship's prison

explanation.surface: A jail and one of the people locked inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a bandit is only maybe a prisoner; the definition leans on the jail just named.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandit or outlaw, the sort of criminal who might end up locked in a prison.

clue.text: Delicate, it is knocked over, found in seven pieces

indicators.note: the reversed words are located inside the other piece
the word seven broken in pieces is rearranged
something knocked over is upended, so the letters run backwards

explanation.surface: A fragile object is knocked over and shatters into seven bits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked over' turns IT IS backwards and 'pieces' rearranges SEVEN to SENVE; 'found in' puts the turned pair inside that. The surface pictures something fragile breaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sensitive is delicate, easily affected or damaged.

clue.text: Confection removed from feast rudely

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the run of the words feast rudely

explanation.surface: A sweet is snatched rudely from a banquet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed from' takes the letters out of feaST RUDELy.
explanation.definitionFit: Strudel is a layered pastry dessert, a sweet confection.

clue.text: Hamlet needs to take offensive without delay

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for offensive goes round the other

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's prince must attack at once, not procrastinate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense of outside. Hamlet looks like Shakespeare's prince, but it is a small settlement; 'needs to take' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamlet is a small settlement, a little village.

clue.text: Share I had in disreputable enterprise

indicators.note: the contracted I had sits inside the dive

parts.note: a dive is a seedy bar or club
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone owns part of a shady business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; 'Share' is a verb, not a portion of the business.
explanation.definitionFit: To divide something is to share it out.

clue.text: Indication of praiseworthy act or indication of wrong-doing

definitions.meaning: an official commendation, as for bravery
a summons, as for a traffic offence

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a formal commendation and a summons to court for an offence.

clue.text: Tangles or untangles

definitions.meaning: entangles threads into a knot
unpicks or frays threads apart

explanation.definitionFit: The verb ravel means both to entangle and to unravel threads.

clue.text: Spirit matured finally in very special oak

indicators.note: the letter from matured sits within the other letters
special treatment rearranges the letters of oak
finally picks the last letter of matured

explanation.surface: A spirit aged at last in a very special oak barrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'special' rearranges OAK into OKA; with V that makes VOKA, and 'in' places D (the last letter of 'matured', picked by 'finally') inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Vodka is a distilled alcoholic spirit.

clue.text: Permitted or penalized

definitions.meaning: officially approved or authorised
punished with sanctions, as a country is

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to authorise and to impose penalties on.

clue.text: Approach or pull away

definitions.meaning: come nearer, as in the end ... near
drag or withdraw, as in ... a curtain back

explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers moving nearer, as in to draw near, and pulling something away.

clue.text: Added fine particles to or removed fine particles from

definitions.meaning: sprinkled with a powder, as a cake with sugar
wiped clean of dirt

explanation.definitionFit: The verb dust means both to sprinkle powder over and to wipe powder off.

clue.text: Become attached or separate

definitions.meaning: stick fast, cling
split apart

explanation.definitionFit: The verb has two opposed senses: to cling to, and to split asunder.
